To expand Bede people’s economic opportunities, the Uttaran Foundation, a local NGO, has trained about 200 young Bede women, who now work in garment factories.
While both aforementioned studies are hyper-local and may not apply to all settlements, they reflect a tension between modern life, environmental realities, and traditions.
The Dhaka University study notes that many Bede families are landless and lack official citizenship documents, which limits their access to relief and disaster programs.

items.title: How a civic tech platform is helping women in Serbia get home safely

s: ‘[W]hat can we change in the spaces where people live, work, study and spend their free time?’

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South.
It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.
For many women and girls in Serbia, safety is not only a question of physical protection.
It influences their freedom of movement, their choices, and their ability to participate equally in public life.
This issue cannot be viewed separately from the broader social position of women and young people.

Reports by the Youth Umbrella Organisation of Serbia (KOMS) show that many young people experience insecurity, declining trust in institutions, and limited opportunities for meaningful participation in decisions that affect their lives.
The reports also document concerning cases of pressure, threats, and security risks faced by young activists who publicly advocate for social change.

At the same time, reports of the Commissioner for the Protection of Equality highlight that gender-based discrimination and unequal treatment remain persistent challenges in Serbian society, affecting women and girls in various aspects of their everyday lives.
Many incidents of harassment, intimidation, or discomfort in public spaces never become official complaints.
Some women do not believe reporting will lead to change.

Others fear judgment, social stigma, or consider their experience too minor to be important — but no experience is too small when it concerns the right to dignity, freedom of movement, and equal access to public spaces.
Global Voices conducted an email interview with Varvara Lazarevic, the head of an NGO in Novi Sad, Serbia, to find out what can be done about this universal problem.

The NGO, Omladina JAZAS Novi Sad, and their project, SafeSteps, a civic technology platform where women can anonymously share their experiences of insecurity in public spaces, are presented here as an Impact Spotlight for the Serbian edition of the Digital Sparks Program.
Global Voices (GV): Please tell us about your organization and why you chose to get involved with the Digital Sparks project.

Varvara Lazarevic ( VL): Omladina JAZAS Novi Sad has been working with young people and different marginalized groups for many years, with a focus on improving quality of life through education, information and support.

We founded Omladinske novine, a youth media outlet with both print and online editions, and since last year, we have also had our own podcast studio, where we work with young people and teach them about journalism, social media and media production.

Digital Sparks was important to us because it gave us the opportunity to connect areas we have been working on for years — communication, human rights and youth work — with technology. and turn them into a practical tool.
This is how Safe Steps was created.
The idea had been developing for years through my professional work, research and work with young people and women.
I wanted to explore how technology could become genuinely useful to people and give visibility to experiences that often remain unheard.
GV: What issue/challenge in your community prompted you to undertake this project?

items.title: Anthropic exposes AI operation that DRC journalists never knew existed

s: Disinformation surrounding DRC-Rwanda relations has weakened the diplomatic and public standing of both countries
Featured image from DRC media, created using screenshots from ACP's YouTube channel
In September 2026, Anthropic, an artificial intelligence (AI) development and research company, exposed a network of fake news sites targeting the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

The investigation revealed that large-scale, AI-powered disinformation campaigns have emerged at a time of conflict when trust in the news is already at an all-time low and resources are severely limited.
This revelation rang alarm bells for African media watchdogs.
The network coordinated around 70 AI-powered fake news sites and generated at least 318 articles on the eastern DRC conflict, relations with Rwanda, and contested mineral resources.
The operation was highly robust.
On X, coordinated accounts amplified content from the AI-run sites, mimicking legitimate media outlets and rewriting articles for different audiences.
According to Anthropic’s report, the LKM Company, a French advertising agency serving clients with strong interests in the DRC-Rwanda conflict, was behind it all.
They found no evidence of direct government involvement.

When Global Voices approached Hobab Watukalusu, a fact-checker, editor, and head of the training and research department at Soma Média Lab in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, he shared:
Nous n’avions pas identifié cette opération dans toute son ampleur avant sa révélation.

Cela montre les limites auxquelles nous sommes confrontés face à des campagnes capables de produire, à très grande échelle et dans des délais très courts, des contenus qui peuvent paraître crédibles et s’insérer rapidement dans l’écosystème informationnel.
We hadn’t recognized the full extent of the operation before this revelation.
This highlights our limitations when dealing with campaigns that can rapidly generate large-scale, credible-looking content and quickly gain a foothold in the infoscape.
He added that local journalists on the front lines are struggling to keep up as new technologies make it easier than ever to facilitate massive disinformation campaigns.
DR Congolese fact-checkers face a litany of obstacles in slowing disinformation flows across regions.
Hobab outlines the fundamental constraints:
L'accès encore difficile à l'électricité, à une connexion Internet stable et abordable, ainsi que le coût élevé de la vie constituent des contraintes réelles pour les professionnels de l'information.
Ongoing difficulties in accessing electricity, stable and affordable internet connections, and high living costs pose real-world constraints for journalists.
In the DRC, where journalists are already overwhelmed by covering an active military conflict, analyzing potential industrial-scale, AI-generated content is virtually impossible.
Joël Kaseso, another journalist covering disinformation narratives, told Global Voices:
Des ressources existent, mais la plupart sont payantes.
Ce qui limite notre capacité à tout analyser dans ce contexte tendu où les relations diplomatiques et sécuritaires avec les pays voisins, notamment le Rwanda, ne sont plus au bon fixe.
Although resources exist, most are not free.

Amid this tense environment, where diplomatic and security relations with neighboring countries, particularly Rwanda, are strained, this financial barrier limits our ability to conduct a full analysis.

Kaseso has also identified a simple but critical methodology that most journalists use to navigate this situation: analyzing the author’s intentions, the source’s profile (anonymous accounts versus identifiable influencers), and amplification patterns.
However, this requires time and tools that many newsrooms don’t have.
Détecter qu'un contenu a été généré ou manipulé à l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle ne constitue que la première étape.
Il faut ensuite déterminer si ce contenu est trompeur, identifier sa source, comprendre comment il se diffuse et, surtout, établir dans quel objectif il a été produit.
C'est cette chaîne complète de vérification qui demande du temps, des compétences et des ressources.
Detecting AI-generated or AI-manipulated content is only the first step.
The next steps involve determining whether the content is misleading, identifying its source, understanding how it spreads, and, above all, establishing why it was created in the first place.
This comprehensive verification process requires time, skill, and resources.

items.title: Students air their frustrations anonymously online as emigration tempts many young people in North Macedonia

s: ‘Students don’t have to be members of a political party to create change,’ says founder of online media platform

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South.
It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.
Students in North Macedonia are not the happiest group: a 2026 survey suggests that over 76 percent of current students are thinking of emigrating.
The main reasons for this being cited are “quality of life” and “finding employment suitable to professional qualifications.”
However, what if students themselves could change that?
North Macedonia, luckily, has people who decided to take their fate into their own hands and help students achieve a better quality of life, not only for themselves, but for many young people.

At first, Goshe Nikolov, at the time a student himself, founded Instagram-based student media, Studentarija, as an entertainment resource, where students from all over the country shared memes about studies and current events.
This outlet now has over 65,000 subscribers, which is a significant number for a country with 53,000 students.

As he comes to the Zoom interview with Global Voices, Nikolov already has nine years of experience running the most successful student media in the country, and with the help of his team of three, has launched a Digital Student Voice, an online platform that enables students across North Macedonia to anonymously report problems related to higher education and student life.
They were able to do it with the help of the Digital Democracy Initiative grant.
Nikolov has a wide smile and a confident attitude; he answers questions with the clarity that could only be gained by years of hands-on experience.
Global Voices (GV): Could you tell us a little about your student media outlet?
How did it start?
How did you manage to gain so many followers and so much engagement?
Is it only on Instagram?
Goshe Nikolov (GN): Studentarija started in 2017, when I was still a student.
I created it from my room in a student dormitory in Skopje.
At that time, Instagram was becoming increasingly popular among students in North Macedonia, but there was no Macedonian Instagram page specifically for students.
So I decided to create one, and quite spontaneously, in the end it got the name Studentarija, which it still has today.
In the beginning, the idea was very simple.
It was a place where students could share funny and relatable content.
For example, memes, funny videos, everyday posts and situations from student life.
So I could never have imagined that one day it would become what it is today.
Over time, the audience kept growing, and I think that demonstrated that there was a real need for such a space.
At the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, in 2020, I started focusing more on the real problems and challenges faced by students in North Macedonia.
Students started coming to us with questions, asking for information and sharing their problems, because they often could not get the information or support they needed elsewhere.
That was when I really understood that Studentarija could play a much bigger role in the lives of students and young people in our country.
So I think the main reasons young people have stayed with us over the years are our openness, transparency, creativity, consistency and, of course, accessibility.
Students in North Macedonia know that they can come directly to us, that we listen to them, and that Studentarija is genuinely built around their experiences and their needs.
GV: So do you think it will remain only on Instagram, or are you planning to use other platforms for further development?

items.title: Activists push for Pakistan to recognise and support people with albinism

s: Pakistan keeps no data on people with albinism, leaving needs unmet in schools, healthcare, and jobs.
Graph from the 2021 study “ Genetic Causes of Oculocutaneous Albinism in Pakistani Population. ” Sajid et al., Genes 2021, 12(4), 492.
CC BY 4.0 via MDPI.

For Adeel Nasir, 24, who has albinism and lives in Kot Radha Kishan, a town in Kasur district, Punjab Province of Pakistan, school meant constant adjustment to challenges that many people around him did not understand.
Because of low vision, he struggled to read what was written on classroom whiteboards.
Some teachers seated him closer to the board, improved the lighting, and gave him written notes.
But one classroom incident remained painful.
Adeel once asked a teacher what qualifications a fighter pilot needs.
He expected encouragement about his ambition.
Instead, he received a response focused on his eyesight.
“First of all, you should be able to see clearly with your eyes,” Adeel recalled the teacher saying.
His classmates laughed.
Years later, he says people still notice his condition before they recognise his abilities.
“My abilities, my degrees, and my skills were ignored because of my weak eyesight and physical appearance,” he said during an in-person interview with Global Voices.

Adeel’s experience reflects a concern that Malooka-Anne Miti-Drummond, the UN Independent Expert on the enjoyment of human rights by persons with albinism, raised during her June 2026 visit to Pakistan.
She said policies, programmes, and data systems overlook people with albinism.
Albinism is a rare, non-contagious, genetically inherited condition caused by reduced or absent production of melanin, the pigment responsible for colour in the skin, hair, and eyes.
Reduced melanin can result in visual impairment and increased vulnerability to ultraviolet (UV) radiation because melanin provides natural protection against sun damage.
People with albinism are born with the condition; it is not contagious and does not affect their intellectual ability.
Pakistan has no separate national estimate of how many people with albinism live in the country.
The UN notes that country-level data on albinism is scarce worldwide, and many countries collect no official statistics on it.
Available estimates put prevalence at roughly one in 17,000 to 20,000 people in many European and North American populations, and higher in some African communities.
The UN has called for better data collection to understand the challenges people with albinism face.
The absence of a national estimate does not mean that people with albinism are absent in Pakistan.
Researchers have documented albinism among Pakistani families despite the missing estimate.

A study of 94 previously unreported Pakistani families with non-syndromic oculocutaneous albinism found disease-causing variants mainly in the TYR and OCA2 genes, two of the major genetic causes of albinism worldwide.
Genetic studies of affected families cannot establish how many people with albinism live in the country.
For Adeel, the lack of recognition shapes how institutions treat his needs.

After a long effort, he obtained a disability certificate, but as he explained, “The disability certificate we received is also issued on the basis of our weak eyesight, not because of albinism itself.”
“There is no place in any office or government institution where a separate form or category under the name of ‘albino’ exists where we can register ourselves,” Adeel added.
The difficulty of documenting albinism ties to a broader gap in disability data.
Many national systems measure disability through functional difficulties and do not record each medical condition separately.
Pakistan’s 2023 Population and Housing Census asked about difficulty seeing, hearing, walking, communicating, remembering, and caring for oneself rather than individual conditions.
A Pakistan Bureau of Statistics representative, who spoke to Global Voices on condition of anonymity, said the bureau keeps no separate official data on people with albinism.
The person said collecting information on rare conditions requires well-designed questionnaires, and Pakistan would have to choose the best method before adding albinism to future data collection.

items.title: At the UN, plans for a global coalition to attack LGBTQ+ and reproductive rights

s: Far-right activists are trying to dismantle global protections for LGBTQ+ people under the guise of ‘family values’
US President Trump speaking at the U.N.
General Assembly.
Photo by The White House. Fair use.
This article by Hope Pisoni was originally published by Uncloseted Media, an LGBTQ+ focused investigative news outlet, on October 1, 2026.
An edited version is being republished on Global Voices as part of a content partnership agreement.
It has been edited for length and style.

On September 17, while the United Nations (U.N.) was hosting its annual General Assembly for diplomats and leaders from all over the world, several key figures filled a room across the street at the Millennium Hilton in Midtown Manhattan.
Attendees included Trump administration officials, leaders of anti-LGBTQ+ hate groups, far-right politicians from Latin America and reporters from far-right media.

These people were meeting for the Global Forum for Life, Family and Freedoms, a two-day summit of right-wing leaders with an ambitious goal to create a new “pro-life and pro-family” Core Group at the U.N.
Since 2008, the U.N. has had an LGBTI Core Group with 42 member states whose mission is to advocate for LGBTQ+ rights on a global stage.
But the organizers of this new group hope to create an opposing organization to push for policies that undermine reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights around the globe.

Aarón Lara, the Mexico-based conservative activist who came up with the idea for the group, said in an August article that the existing LGBTI Core Group has only been successful because there has not been organized conservative opposition, which a new core group would provide.
Lara (left) speaking with a reporter in the Dominican Republic in March.
Screenshot via Central Noticias YouTube.

“[The LGBTI Core Group] has successfully established victimhood narratives and incorporated observances with global impact. … I always use this example: If it were a soccer match and one team failed to show up, the winner by default would be the team that was present,” Lara said.
Lara and other supporters of the group agreed at the forum to draw up plans for its creation in the coming months.

They may be encouraged to move quickly because the group’s leaders have said they want to use the U.S.’s global influence and capitalize on the current administration’s anti-LGBTQ and anti-abortion stance to do it.
The U.S. recently left the LGBTI Core Group, an early move by Trump in his second term.
The LGBTI Core Group describes itself as “an informal cross-regional group of United Nations Member States.

While it is not an official U.N. body, its work includes ensuring that LGBTQ+ people are considered and protected across all of the U.N.’s activities, from humanitarian aid to human rights resolutions.
For example, one of the first U.N. resolutions to reference LGBTQ+ people was one protecting civilians against extrajudicial executions.
When some members tried to remove LGBTQ people from those protections, advocates and allies fought to keep them in place.

Maria Sjödin, executive director of Outright International, an NGO that focuses on supporting LGBTQ rights worldwide, told Uncloseted Media that work like this could be in jeopardy should the new core group come to fruition.

“We’re talking about the protection of some very basic human rights, and that the opposition to that is trying to organize to make it even more difficult to pass such a thing is really quite horrible,” she says.
Core groups are not official U.N. bodies, so there is no strictly required procedure for their creation.

While there have been other core groups established at the U.N., the LGBTI group is unique in that it is designed for continuous operation on multiple issues rather than as a response to a specific conflict or crisis.
The “pro-life, pro-family” core group would change that, threatening to shift the balance of power at the U.N.

items.title: How an extremist network articulated a hoax linking Brazil’s President Lula to child abuse on X

s: Monitoring of 1,819 posts showed far-right users tried to manipulate Grok, X’s AI tool
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
Art by: Méuri Elle/Aos Fatos, used with permission.

A few days before the first round of the 2026 general elections in Brazil on October 4, it took only a few hours for a line said by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva about preventive exams for prostate cancer to be twisted into a pedophilia accusation against him.
Aos Fatos obtained and checked 1,819 posts on X (formerly Twitter), which reconstructed how this hoax was planted and harvested by Bolsonarista users on social media between September 28 and 29.

The distortion in the meaning of Lula’s speech stemmed from a false pedophilia accusation that had already been boosted hours ahead of a statement he made at a campaign event in the city of Belém, Pará state, on September 28.
Users manipulated questions asked to Grok, X’s AI assistance tool, to make it state “Lula consumes CP” — an acronym in English for child pornography.
The chatbot warned that the sentence was wordplay and that it had no records to support the claim.
However, the edit cut from Lula’s speech, shared on social media, gave the narrative new momentum.

Besides requests to make the video viral and to mobilize influencers, some publications also revived old episodes and characters without any connection to Lula’s line to back theories associating the president with child abuse.

During his rally, Lula was talking about the importance of cancer prevention and criticizing men’s resistance to having prostate exams, compared to women’s healthcare culture, which, according to him, is used to having gynecological exams from an early age.

Among the publications with broader reach identified by the survey, one of the first to cut a quote from Lula’s speech was posted at 11.59 p.m. on September 28 by Pâm, an influencer, founder of a Bolsonarista site called The Incorrupt, and member of Estúdio 5, a pro-Bolsonaro content-making hub aligned with Catholicism.
A user identified as Pâm posted: ‘Lula saying women ‘learn to be touched ever since they are little’ WHAT THE FUCK, PRESIDENT?
Are you NUTS???.
Image: Screenshot from X. Fair use.
At 12.28 a.m. on September 29, the Space Liberdade account published another cut from the same quote.
It took only a minute for the interpretation to be turned into an explicit accusation.
At 12.29 a.m., two other posts were already calling the president “a pedophile”; one of them requesting users to pass this claim along.
In the following hours, several users started acting to amplify the reach of the accusation.
Posts asked people to download and repost the video, suggested boosting the hashtag #LULAPEDOPHILE, and included messages like “it has to go viral.
At 2.48 a.m., a profile proposed to pick out two sentences from Lula’s speech, create a hashtag, and mobilize 10 to 20 influencers around it.
An account called Space Liberdade posted: ‘URGENT — Lula says men don’t like ‘to be touched’ and states that women learn ‘to be touched’ since they are little.
(…) a man doesn’t; he doesn’t know that once he has prostate cancer they will touch him a lot.
Image: Screenshot from X. Fair use.

Five hours before Pâm’s publication, users connected to the so-called “bolha da resenha” (hangout banter bubble) were already experimenting with Grok, forcing the tool to associate Lula with pedophilia.

The term describes an ecosystem of profiles, most of them anonymous, that combine aggressive humour, extremist political content, and reproducing chans aesthetics — anonymous forums well known as one of the main cradles of the current far-right.

items.title: Peru’s Indigenous people in Cutivireni and Oviri take the front line against Amazon wildfires

s: Indigenous guardians play a critical role in protecting the land, their homes, and their livelihoods

The Cool Earth initiative in Cutivireni and Oviri works around three key concepts: the monitoring of satellite fire weather alerts, the introduction of a flag-based system regarding safe times to conduct traditional fire practices, and practical training to contain small blazes and prevent them from causing devastation to the Indigenous people in the rainforest.
Photo by Cool Earth, 2026; used with permission.
It’s September and 2026 has already been defined by wildfires spanning across the globe.
Driven by the heat and dryness of the climate crisis, outbursts on the edge of Bordeaux, France have forced 200,000 from their homes and led to deaths in Spain.
Smoke has billowed across the Canada-U.S. border, covering cities in smog.

Fires are expected to continue as seasons transition in the Southern Hemisphere, with a severe El Niño phenomenon that the United Nations warns will add pressure to an already scorching globe, risking similar conditions to those that — back in 2024 — drove the worst Amazonian wildfires in two decades.

With fire and drought risks set to increase in the coming months, Indigenous people in the Amazon rainforest are stepping up to take on new roles as fire brigade members, protecting both their homes and a key natural resource in the fight against climate change.

Ahead of this year’s El Niño weather pattern, Indigenous people from Peru’s Cutivireni and Oviri communities approached Cool Earth: they wanted to ensure they were equipped to fight any fires this coming season.

The organization’s long-established relationship with the two Indigenous groups and experience working with the Central Asháninka of the Ene River to create the Paamari programme, made it easier to establish four fire crews across communities that were already springing into action.
In Cutivireni, the newly formed Chullachaqui fire crew have faced multiple blazes.
Named after an Amazonian forest spirit, the crew understand the critical role they play in protecting the land, their homes, and their livelihoods.

In early August came one of the first tests of their training: alerted by people in the Tsyapo and Pajonal communities, community brigade members joined up with their partners in Central Cutivireni to tackle the fire, which they successfully put out.

Julio Acosta, Cool Earth’s Forest Data Manager, said that the organization really admires and appreciates how the communities have been making the best use of what they have been building with them, adding, “This early action taken in Tsyapo and Pajonal demonstrates how effectively they put into practice what they’ve learned in the workshops.”
The training was taken directly from concepts in the Paamari programme.

Similar to Paamari, the Cool Earth initiative with Cutivireni and Oviri works around three key concepts: the increased monitoring of satellite fire weather alerts, the introduction of a flag-based system regarding safe times to conduct traditional fire practices, and practical training to contain small blazes and prevent them from causing devastation to the Indigenous people in the rainforest.
The communities themselves often act as the brigade’s eyes, alerting them to smoke or flames.

Working in close coordination with local authorities, brigade members first assess the wildfires and try to tame the blazes in their initial stage, before they require a more complex response by the authorities.
Acosta stressed the importance of highlighting the fact that the main work of these brigades lies in prevention, rather than initial response.
“This tends to be less visible,” he explained, {but the measures they take, such as the flag system, help reduce the occurrence of these fires.
Seeing the initiative and eagerness to learn more from the brigade members motivates us to expand and improve the work we’ve been implementing together.”

items.title: Hong Kong police launch AI-powered national security platform for school pupils

s: ‘May the seeds of national security take root and sprout in the hearts of the pupils…’
Hong Kong police launch an AI-powered national security education platform for the city’s pupils during a ceremony on October 6, 2026.
Photo: HKPF, via Facebook.
Used with permission.
Hong Kong police have launched an artificial intelligence-powered national security education platform for young students.

The NSmarties AI Interactive Platform was officially launched on October 6, 2026, at a ceremony at Precious Blood Primary School in Ap Lei Chau, with about 700 pupils attending, police said in a Facebook post:

【 NSmarties童心護港AI互動平台 • 正式啟動 】 國家安全，由童心出發！ 由警務處國家安全處主辦的「NSmarties童心護港AI互動平台」今日（6日）於海怡寶血小學正式啟動！ 警務處處長周一鳴、警務處副處長（國家安全）江學禮、寶血會總會長區綺雯修女等一眾嘉賓，聯同約700位同學一同見證這個重要時刻。 啟動禮圓滿結束，標誌着國安教育以創新科技走進校園的新里程！ 願國安種子在同學心裏生根發芽，茁壯成長！
[ NSmarties: Children’s Hearts Protect Hong Kong AI Interactive Platform • Officially Launched ] National security begins with the hearts of children!

Organized by the National Security Department of the Hong Kong Police Force, the ‘NSmarties: Children’s Hearts Protect Hong Kong AI Interactive Platform’ was officially launched today (6th) at Sea View Precious Blood Primary School!

Distinguished guests, including Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming, Deputy Commissioner of Police (National Security) Kelvin Kong Hok-lai, and Sister Au Yee-man, President of the Precious Blood Society, joined some 700 pupils in witnessing this momentous occasion.
The successful launch ceremony marks a new milestone in bringing national security education into schools through innovative technology!
May the seeds of national security take root and sprout in the hearts of the pupils, and grow strong!

The platform, jointly developed by police and Hong Kong Qianfan Technology, lets students generate personalized stories centered on China’s “holistic approach to national security” — a framework pushed by Chinese President Xi Jinping that covers areas from politics and the economy to ecology and technology.
It also features the voices of Chow and security chief Chris Tang, who explain the city’s national security laws and security information.
The ceremony marked a “milestone” in bringing national security education into the city’s schools through innovative technologies, police said.
The NSmarties platform was first unveiled on National Security Education Day in April, but it was not fully launched to the public at that time.
Hong Kong has strengthened national security education alongside a crackdown since Beijing imposed a national security law in 2020 following the 2019 protests and unrest.
Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest.
It criminalized subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts — broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure.
The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents, while dozens of civil society groups disappeared.
The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners, the UN and NGOs.

items.title: Norway’s Telenor telecom faces lawsuit for giving user data to Myanmar junta

s: The state-owned company is accused of abetting crimes against humanity
Telenor telecom operated in Myanmar from 2014 to 2022.
Photo by Bjoertvedt.
Source: Wikipedia.
CC BY-SA 4.0
The Norway-based multinational telecom company Telenor is facing charges for its role in turning over sensitive customer data to the military government of Myanmar.
If successful, the case would be the first ever to hold a telecom company accountable for failing to protect user data from being misused by an authoritarian regime.
Telenor operated in Myanmar from 2014 to 2022 with 18 million subscribers.
After the February 2021 coup, Telenor faced pressure after the junta demanded compliance with its surveillance and content blocking directives.
Telenor decided to leave Myanmar, but civil society groups raised strong objections that its local operations would be sold to a company with links to the junta.
In December 2024, activist group Justice For Myanmar filed a complaint against Telenor in Norway for breach of the Sanctions Act.
Norway rejected it, but the complaint was refiled in October 2025 with an additional charge of aiding and abetting crimes against humanity.
The Norwegian state has a 54-percent stake in Telenor.
In December 2025, the Norwegian Parliament initiated an investigation into the operations of Telenor in Myanmar.

The leader of the disciplinary committee of the Parliament said: “We must uncover how a state-owned company could cooperate with a brutal military regime (by handing over) customer information about the opposition [in Myanmar].”
In April 2026, a civil class action lawsuit was filed against Telenor in Norway by Myanmar citizens for sharing their sensitive personal data with the junta.
The complaint alleged that Telenor shared at least 1,253 phone numbers with the regime.
The data also included call logs and location data, names, addresses, ID numbers, Facebook, and bank accounts linked to mobile numbers.
Among the complainants is Tha Zin, the widow of rapper and lawmaker Phyo Zeya Thaw, who was arrested based on a trumped-up charge, convicted, and later executed by the junta.
Tha Zin said her husband was arrested right after his account information was accessed by the junta.
I lost my husband.
It is not just a wife losing her husband.
It is also a loss to the movement.
It is also a loss to democracy because my husband was committed to democracy and a youth leader.
Losing him means a loss to the country.
Lawyer Jan Magne Langseth summed up the content of the complaint.
Telenor ASA in Norway clearly contributed to the practice of handing over user data, despite the inherent risks for its customers in Myanmar.
We have evidence of cases where the team at HQ expressly recommended the data to be handed over.
In September 2026, Norway’s National Criminal Investigation Service and the interior security service searched the office of Telenor related to the charges filed against the company.
Justice for Myanmar spokesperson Yadanar Maung welcomed the decision of Norway authorities to investigate Telenor.
Telenor’s transfer of spyware to a military-linked company and sharing of sensitive data with the military junta was extensively documented
We hope this will finally lead to accountability for the harms Telenor has caused Myanmar people through its conduct and its dangerous divestment.
In several statements sent to the media, Telenor said it is cooperating with authorities with regard to the ongoing investigation.
It added that it needed to defend its employees in Myanmar.
In Myanmar, refusing requests from the military authorities could, in the worst case, have led to imprisonment, torture or the death penalty.
Telenor Myanmar had no real options.
We could not play Russian roulette with the lives of our employees.
Telenor media relations director David Fidjeland reiterated the same point.
Our employees risked imprisonment, torture or the death penalty if the military authorities’ orders were not complied with.
We found that we had no real choice and that we could not put our employees’ lives at risk.

items.title: How authoritarian states are building an international market for digital surveillance

s: The main danger of AI in authoritarian regimes is the ability to suppress any protest
Moscow subway cameras are connected to a facial recognition system.
Screenshot taken from the YouTube video “Facial recognition cameras help detain dissidents in the Moscow metro” by the DW YouTube channel; fair use.
Sonya, from Stavropol Krai, Russia, is 15 years old.
In June 2026, she was sentenced to 70 hours of compulsory labor, connected to a February 2026 incident in which she had written the surname “Navalny” on a bus stop.
That stop happened to be in a district that was being monitored by officers from the Center for Combating Extremism, commonly called Center E.
Similarly, Yuri, a pensioner from Astrakhan who was also identified from surveillance footage, was given three years of restricted freedom for writing “No to War” in red marker on buildings.
Authoritarian regimes are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) as a technology of political survival.

Cameras with facial recognition, video analytics, biometric databases, digital IDs, social media monitoring, Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) systems, and public service platforms are gradually merging into a single infrastructure of control.
Such a system makes it possible not only to observe citizens in real time, but also to reconstruct their past movements, connections, habits, communications, and political activity.

The main risk is that AI and related technologies make repression faster and less visible: the state no longer needs to constantly demonstrate force if citizens know they can be identified retroactively.
Modern digital authoritarianism is not developing in isolation, but through the international exchange of technologies, standards, and practices.

China, Russia, Iran, Belarus, Venezuela, countries in Africa, Western and Central Asia, and companies connected to them, sell and exchange AI infrastructure tools that are being used for the purpose of repression.
Western technologies a re also being bought and exchanged within authoritarian regimes.

In early June 2026, Sberbank Deputy Chairman Alexander Vedyakhin told Reuters that the company was offering countries in the Global South access to Russian AI models that would take “local values” into account.
Vedyakhin was referring to specific large language models (LLMs) — GigaChat and YandexGPT — which Russia had been trying to develop since 2019.
However, as IT expert Alexander Isavnin told journalists at the podcast Zhivoy Gvozd, Russian generative AI models lag behind American and Chinese models and cannot even generate text in Cyrillic.

Yet, new national and sovereign AI models are supposed to reflect traditional values, including patriotism, service to the Fatherland and responsibility for its fate, a strong family, historical memory and continuity between generations, and unity of the peoples of Russia.
These models are expected to be trained on domestic, authentically Russian material.

It is reasonable to assume that in countries like those in Western Asia, Russian AI models will reflect adherence to Islamic traditions, while in Argentina, perhaps, they will reflect respect for football from an early age.

Developers, meanwhile, do not understand how people with no idea about how any of this works can write AI laws: “In places, the document reads as if it was written by people who had only ever seen LLMs in local news.
From the perspective of global democracy, however, this illiteracy among Russian lawmakers suggests that Russia is unlikely to supply LLMs to autocracies around the world.
China, by contrast — unlike American developers — makes its language models open in principle, meaning that anyone can take the code and modify it for their own needs.

In China, all LLMs are controlled and tightly regulated by the state, so party censorship is written into the code from the start — for example, you cannot get an answer about the Tiananmen Square protests.
However, the models are distributed as open source, which is why more than 50 percent of Chinese model users come from developers, including those in the Global South.

items.title: Musique Libre Femmes plays for Women's History Month at Tompkins Square Library in New York City

s: On Thursday, March 12, 2026, the Tompkins Square Library in New York City hosted a concert by Musique Libre Femmes, in its basement performance space.
This performance featured Cheryl Pyle on flute, Ayumi Ishito on saxophones, and Roberta Piket on piano.
There were approximately fifteen people in attendance.
Wikinews attended the event and took several photos and recordings to transcribe for this news report.
The performance started at 6:00 p.m.
New York Time (2200 UTC), and was introduced by director of adult services Jeffrey Katz.
After explaining that the series was ongoing, and announcing upcoming performance dates as well, he introduced the performers:
((Jeffrey Katz)) So we are celebrating Women's History Month with Musique Libre Femmes.
And this is a group of all women free jazz improvisers who compose, create spontaneous, in-the-moment music.
The group consists of some of the most experienced improvisers of the New York Jazz scene.
And they have recently played at the Lady Got Chops Festival, the Downtown Music Gallery, and many of the New York City Jazz venues.
After which, the performance began and lasted about forty minutes, after which the audience applauded.
After the event, Pyle had the following comments about the series:

((Cheryl Pyle)) I started the group Musique Libre Femmes, Free Music Women, because I saw a film called Fire Music, and they interviewed Carla Bley and Ingrid Sertso, and they didn't talk about any of their music.
And they didn't talk about any other women improvisers, Barbara Donald, you know, anybody.
So I wanted to do some concerts with all women.
((CP)) And today we played with Roberta Piket on piano and Ayumi Ishito on tenor sax and soprano sax and myself, Cheryl Pyle on C-flute, piccolo and alto flute.
And we're here at the Tompkins Square Library in the East Village and we just had a wonderful concert.

items.title: United States announces blockade on the Strait of Hormuz

s: On Sunday, United States President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US is imposing a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
According to Trump, the blockade was in effect as of 10:00 a.m.
Eastern Time (1400 UTC).
The blockade was imposed following the collapse of talks held in Islamabad between the United States and Iran.
"Effective immediately, the United States Navy, the finest in the world, will be BLOCKADING any and all ships trying to enter, or leave, the Strait of Hormuz," Trump declared.
According to The Guardian, oil prices briefly rose above US$100 a barrel following news of the blockade, before easing back to just over US$99; gas prices also increased.
Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X to "Enjoy the current pump figures.
With the so-called 'blockade', soon you'll be nostalgic for $4–$5 gas.
He further stated that Iran would respond in kind to both escalation and diplomacy, warning that it would "fight" if confronted militarily but would "deal with logic" if approached constructively.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed hope that the ceasefire would remain stable, stating that Beijing is willing to cooperate with all parties to "guarantee the uninterrupted flow of energy supplies," and that stability in the Strait of Hormuz is critically important to China.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV visits four nations in Africa

s: Pope Leo XIV arrived by plane in Algeria on Monday, April 13, beginning his apostolic visit to Africa.

A senior Vatican official told the BBC the pope wanted to "turn the world's attention to Africa"; the BBC reported the eleven-day visit would address themes of peace, migration, and interfaith dialogue.
The trip also includes stops in Cameroon, Angola, and Equatorial Guinea.
The visit marked Leo's second major foreign trip as pope since his election in May last year.
The regions of the continent being visited are among the quickest growing in Catholicism in the world.
There were an estimated 288 million Catholics in Africa in 2024, making up more than one-fifth of the world's total.
His first stop in Algeria marked the first papal visit to the country in history.
While there, Leo planned to visit several locations including ancient Christian sites in Annaba and the Great Mosque of Algiers in the capital before departing.

The stop was followed by a visit to Cameroon, where Leo addressed about 120,000 people in Douala, encouraging young people to turn away from violence and corruption and advocating for justice and peace.
He was expected to make a planned visit to a Catholic hospital in the city before traveling to Yaoundé to meet with students from the Catholic University of Central Africa.
On Sunday, April 19, the pope arrived in Angola, where he met with President João Lourenço and other officials.
He later addressed a crowd gathered near the capital, Luanda.
He was also expected to visit the town of Muxima, the country's main Christian pilgrimage site.

After Angola, the pope arrived on Tuesday, April 21, in Equatorial Guinea, where, according to the BBC, Catholics make up more than 70% of the central African nation, for the final leg of the visit, before his scheduled return to the Vatican.

items.title: Wikimedia Foundation closes Wikinews after 21 years

s: The Board of Trustees of the Wikimedia Foundation announced on March 30 its decision to close all language editions of the project.

In the announcement, a representative from Wikimedia Foundation cited motivations such as "long-term sustainability, levels of community activity, and the availability of reliable news coverage on other platforms".
The announcement stated that all Wikinews editions—referring to the multiple language sections of Wikinews—would "transition to read-only mode" on May 4.
The announcement did not mention the time zone when the wiki would go in read-only mode; but Wikinews operated under the UTC timezone.

In the announcement message, WMF trustee Victoria Doronina said, "We thank all contributors who have participated in Wikinews over the years and helped build a unique experiment in collaborative journalism within the Wikimedia movement.
We understand that some of them may be disappointed by this decision.
To our regret, the project wasn't able to fulfil its promise, and many of its functions were eclipsed by the notable news coverage in Wikipedias."
According to the WMF, most traffic to Wikinews came in the form of web crawlers and bots, as opposed to humans.
Per the Wikimedia Cloud statistics in the past one year, both, English and Chinese Wikinews received more traffic from humans as compared to crawlers.
The foundation stated in its closure recommendation that it is "difficult to claim that it is disseminating educational content and, even more so, that it is doing so effectively and globally."
On March 31, users from different countries and regions started discussions regarding moving the Wikinews content and community to another website at Wikimedia's Meta-Wiki.

Miraheze and Wikimedia NYC were in discussion of continuing the hosting as Wikinews Pulse, with a restructure to increase multilingual support and try new outputs, according to a note by a Wikimedia volunteer User:Pharos.
However, at the time of publishing this report, they had not provided an estimated time the project would be restarted.
Wikinews was a sister project of other Wikimedia initiatives.
Some of the other sister projects includes Wikipedia, Wiktionary, and Wikimedia Commons.
All of these Wikimedia projects support the dissemination of free knowledge and media.
The future of Wikinews was raised for consideration in June, with a WMF task force recommending the project's closure, followed by a period of public consultation about Wikinews.
After this process, the Board announced in March that the 31 active editions of Wikinews would be placed in read-only mode indefinitely.
Wikinews was launched in November 2004.
It was first proposed by an anonymous contributor in January 2003 and faced a community vote that ended 151 yea and 59 nay, leading to the first demo going live in October 2004.
The English-language Wikinews was formally created December 2 of that year, with German following one day later.
The project's early development followed a series of community discussions and milestones in late 2004 and early 2005.
A non-binding straw poll on content licensing began on October 26, 2004, alongside discussions on the project's scope and policies.
The initial demo site, hosted at demo.wikinews.org, was later moved to the English Wikinews domain on December 2 of that year.

Following the launch of the English and German editions in December 2004, additional language editions were created in early 2005, including Dutch, French, Swedish, Spanish, Bulgarian, Polish, Romanian, and Portuguese.
The project also adopted a logo in February 2005 through a community voting process.
While many Wikinews articles were synthesized from other news sources, the project also posted original reporting.
The purpose of this activity was to add exclusive content which would not be available elsewhere on the web or on television.
These original reports included interviews with people such as Shimon Peres, then-president of Israel; U.S.
Senator Sam Brownback; journalist Gay Talese; and voice actor Billy West.
A 2005 article featuring original reporting, Unrest in Belize, was cited by Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales as Wikinews's first scoop.

items.title: Opposition leader Tarique Rahman returns to Bangladesh after 17 years

s: Tarique Rahman, the acting chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) returned to Bangladesh on December 25, 2025, landing in Dhaka after 17 years in self-imposed exile in London.
His arrival marks a significant development in the country's political landscape following the ouster of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August 2024.
Rahman is the son of Khaleda Zia, the official chairperson of the party and former Prime Minister of Bangladesh.
Upon landing at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, Rahman was greeted by thousands of Bangladesh Nationalist Party supporters amid tight security.

Accompanied by his wife, Zubaida Rahman, and daughter, Zaima Rahman, he addressed a rally, emphasizing national unity, inclusivity across religious lines, and the vision of a democratic and economically strong Bangladesh.
He drew parallels to the country's 1971 war of independence.
Rahman, aged 60, left Bangladesh in 2008 for medical treatment after being released on bail following 18 months in detention during the military-backed government's rule from 2006 to 2008.
He was convicted in absentia of charges including corruption, money laundering, and involvement in a 2004 grenade attack on a political rally for his political rival, Sheikh Hasina.
These convictions were overturned or stayed after Hasina's government's fall.
His return comes amid preparations for general elections scheduled for early 2026, under an interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus.
The elections follow a student-led uprising in 2024 that resulted in Hasina's removal and her subsequent flight to India.
The protests, initially sparked by opposition to a job quota system, escalated into broader anti-government demonstrations, leading to an estimated 1,400 deaths according to United Nations figures.
Hasina has since been sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity related to the crackdown.
According to a December poll by the International Republican Institute, the BNP is the frontrunner for the election with 30 percent support.
The party has recently distanced itself from allies like Jamaat-e-Islami to adopt a more centrist approach.
However, challenges remain, including integrating party factions, maintaining law and order, and addressing potential unrest from Awami League supporters.
The Awami League was not allowed to participate in the elections.
Rahman's mother, Khaleda Zia, 80, is hospitalised in critical condition since November 2025.
She was the BNP's acting chairman since 2018 and was jailed most of the times during Hasina's administration.

items.title: United States capture Venezuelan president, Nicolás Maduro

s: The president of Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, has been captured by the United States on Saturday at around 3 am UTC-4, according to a post by US president Donald Trump on social media.
Trump has told reporters Maduro had been “in a house that was more like a fortress”, in the country’s capital, Caracas.
Trump justified this action by claiming that Maduro is the leader of the Cartel de los Soles, and pushing illegal immigration of dangerous individuals in the United States.
Yván Gil Pinto, Venezuela’s foreign minister, said the country has requested a United Nations Security Council meeting to be held after the attack.
The BBC reports airstrikes in Caracas targeting La Carlota, an airbase and Fort Tiuna, a military base where the United States suspected Maduro to be located, and in other locations.
According to local authorities there has been civilian deaths and injuries, but the exact numbers are still unknown.
It was also reported by the BBC that the operation was orchestrated by a {CIA infiltration of the Venezuelan government.
France 24 reported that the CIA had been monitoring his “every movement since August”, despite Maduro’s efforts to change location regularly.
It was also reported that the operation involved more than 150 military aircraft, including one helicopter that was to capture Maduro.

According to the United States authorities, the Delta Force special operation force, arrived at Maduro’s location at “2:01 a.m. local time” and were able to capture him before he could get into his solid steel safe room (sources contradict however, on his exact location at that point.
Some sources reported that Trump said Maduro was almost in his safe room whilst others said he was sleeping in his bed).
They then relocated the “indicted persons” on a ship after crossing the coastline of Venezuela at 3:29 am.

Trump later revealed that Maduro’s wife, Cilia Flores, was also captured, and both were on board the USS Iwo Jima (LHD-7) with destination the southern district of New York, ultimately to be prosecuted.

Attorney General Pam Bondi was quoted by the BBC saying “[he will] face the full wrath of American justice on American soil in American courts” and, according to CNN, announced an indictment for leading “state‐sponsored gangs” and supporting drug trafficking.
Venezuelan authorities also reported other strikes, said to be made with the intent of seizing their oil and minerals, and have declared national emergency.
They, along with Cuba, Colombia, Iran and Russia, have denounced the action as a “serious military aggression”.
Argentine’s president, Javier Milei supported the action.
Venezuela’s vice‐president, Delcy Rodríguez called for Maduro and his wife to be released, saying the operation violated the country’s territorial integrity.
The BBC stated that these strikes follow a string of more than 30 strikes on Venezuelan vessels, and a strike on a “dock area” in Maracaibo, resulting in the death of more than 110 people.
The Trump administration stated that it is engaging in “non‐international armed conflict with […] alleged drug traffickers”.
According to the BBC, legal experts doubt the legality of these actions, saying the strikes are not against "lawful military targets".
According to CNN, Trump also justified not advising Congress before the operation to avoid a "leak", which drew criticisms from Democratic lawmakers.

After the capture, the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment against Maduro in which Maduro and others were charged with “conspiracy to commit narco‐terrorism and conspiracy to import cocaine”.

According to the BBC, Maduro has denied this and has said before that Trump’s actual goal is to get access to Venezuela’s oil reserves, as indicated by the United States’ confiscation of several oil tankers.

items.title: Kyiv street to be named for former Ukrainian parliament chairman Andriy Parubiy, killed in Lviv

s: A street in Kyiv will be named after the former Speaker of the Parliament Andriy Parubiy, killed in Lviv.
The initiative to commemorate the prominent Ukrainian politician was supported by 57% of participants in a public poll on "Kyiv Digital" application.
On January 1, Maryna Poroshenko, the leader of “European Solidarity”, announced the street name in the Kyiv City Council and on Facebook.
As the result, a section along Mariinsky Park – from Hrushevskoho Street to Parkova Road – will bear the politician's name, named "Andrei Parubia Street".
In December, former President of Ukraine and head of the European Solidarity party Petro Poroshenko asked the residents of Kyiv to support the vote to name the street after Parubiy.
The street had no name at the time of the proposal.
"This place is significant for our team and for Andriy himself — a significant part of his journey is connected with it," Poroshenko said.
On October 1, 2025, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a decree awarding Parubiy the title of Hero of Ukraine.

A petition to award the title of Hero of Ukraine to Parubiy was registered on the presidential website on September 2, gaining 25,000 signatures, which was necessary for the proposal to be considered by President.
The Verkhovna Rada, the Ukrainian parliament, also supported the request.
Parubiy was among several people who were conferred Heroes of Ukraine.
Others were writer Volodymyr Vakulenko and student and footballer Stepan Chubenko.
Poroshenko lauded the decision, recalling that "Parubiy dedicated his entire life to serving Ukraine".
Andriy Parubiy, 54, who served as the Chairman of Verkhovna Rada from 14 April 2016 to 29 August 2019, was shot and killed in Lviv on 30 August 2025.
He died at the scene from injuries.
The killing happened amid the Russian invasion, which started in 2022.
The shooter managed to escape.
Later, Ukrainian authorities detained a suspect, and allege there is a Russian link to the killing.
Parubiy was an active participant of Euromaidan.
He also served as Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council of Ukraine from February till August 2014.
The suspected killer of Ukrainian lawmaker Andriy Parubiy admitted on 2 September his role in the killing.
He claimed to have comitted the crime in an act of "revenge" against the country’s authorities.
He denied having worked with Russian special services.

items.title: "I came to be the manager ... not the coach": Manchester United fire head coach Ruben Amorim

s: On Monday, Manchester United football team fired its coach Ruben Amorim after fourteen months in the role.
Amorim had met with Omar Berrada, chief executive officer of the team, and Jason Wilcox, the team's director of football, on Friday morning.
While discussing his preferred 3-4-3 style, the conversation reportedly quickly spiraled out of control, resulting in Amorim losing his job.
Manchester United announced the news of the dismissal at around 10 a.m. on Monday.
After the team drawing against Leeds F.C.
1-1, the coach had said at a press conference that he came to be "the manager, not the coach" and said Wilcox should "do his job".
Wilcox intended the meeting to focus on the recent draw.

Manchester United was sixth in the Premier League, almost not classifying for the Champions League, less than four points ahead of Sunderland A.F.C., Everton F.C., Fulham F.C., Brighton & Hove Albion F.C., Newcastle United and Brentford F.C., a precarious position, El Pais reported.
Former Manchester United captain Gary Neville communicated to Sky Sports News that he expected better performance, saying he "thought they'd get through another couple of weeks."

items.title: Homeland Security says Minneapolis woman shot by ICE officer dies

s: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) reported Wednesday that a woman shot by a U.S.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in Minneapolis has died.
Homeland Security officials have described the shooting as an act of self-defense, while Minnesota governor Tim Walz and Minneapolis mayor Jacob Frey have pushed back on this account.

DHS spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin stated that the shooting occurred when ICE officers fired "defensive shots" in response to the woman "attempting to run over our law enforcement officers" with her vehicle.
Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem said the woman’s conduct was "an act of domestic terrorism."
The incident was under active investigation, with the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA) and the FBI taking over the case.
Walz said the state was working to learn more and asked residents to remain calm, while protest activity continued at the scene and a substantial law-enforcement presence remained in the area.
According to ABC News, Jacob Frey, the mayor of Minneapolis, said in a statement that he was aware of the shooting and urged the agency to depart the city at once.
On social media, he stated the involvement of federal immigration officers was "causing chaos in our city.
He added that the city is "demanding ICE to leave the city immediately," and said officials "stand rock solid with our immigrant and refugee communities.
In a news conference, he disputed the account that the woman's vehicle was weaponized against the agent.

items.title: Roblox player uncovers cheating, awarded Guinness World Record

s: In early January, international media reported that Quinten Delaere, an 18-year-old, had been officially recognized by Guinness World Records after exposing cheating on the Roblox platform.
Delaere, known online as 'kannotlogin', used data analysis to demonstrate that the top times on the global leaderboard were achieved using illegal scripts.
Delaere was competing in a speed-running event for the game Ultimate Easy Obby.
The event was an official collaboration between Roblox and Guinness World Records.
Players had to complete a digital obstacle course as fast as possible.
According to JV, after weeks of practice, Delaere posted a time of 5 minutes and 48.96 seconds.
Before the competition closed, three unknown accounts posted times around 5 minutes and 42 seconds.
JV reported that Delaere, posting on Reddit, believed the times were humanly impossible.
Delaere conducted a digital forensic analysis and compiled a report alleging that the new records were fraudulent.
The report cited three technical points.
First, the analysis pointed to the timestamps of the badges earned by the rival accounts.
The data showed that badges were unlocked in a non-chronological order.
Delaere’s report described the non-chronological order as consistent with the use of teleportation scripts in a normally linear course.
Second, the top accounts were missing specific digital items in their inventory.
Players who cross the finish line automatically receive a 'digital receipt' (an in-game item).
The suspect accounts lacked this item.
According to Kotaku, Delaere argued that "this proved he never actually touched the finish line trigger; he likely teleported a coordinate script to the end-game lobby."
PCGamesN reported that Delaere’s investigation found expired items in the players’ inventories.
Delaere also submitted a frame-by-frame video analysis of his own run to calculate the theoretical maximum speed, arguing that the rival times were mathematically unachievable.
"I took my best run and calculated the theoretical maximum time save possible (perfect pixels, zero drag).
Even with a TAS (Tool-Assisted Speedrun) level of perfection, the times the cheaters posted were mathematically impossible within the game’s physics engine."
Delaere submitted his findings to the Guinness World Records headquarters in London.
MeriStation reported that, after an internal review, the organization concluded Delaere was correct, disqualified the other accounts, and awarded him the official world record.
The challenged times were removed from the database.
The time set by Delaere was officially recognized as the new world record.

items.title: Grateful Dead rhythm guitarist Bob Weir dies, aged 78

s: On Saturday, the family of American musician and songwriter Bob Weir announced that he had died surrounded by loved ones.
The former guitarist and vocalist of the rock band Grateful Dead was 78.
His family announced his death via Instagram, noting that he had recently fought a cancer diagnosis but died due to "underlying lung issues".
The announcement did not specify the date of Weir's death.

Weir played rhythm guitar and sang with American psychedelic rock band the Grateful Dead for decades, and also wrote some of their songs, including the hit "Sugar Magnolia", a staple of Grateful Dead concerts.
He also had a long solo career, making various groups with fellow Grateful Dead alumni, and playing live until months before his death.

Weir was born Robert Hall Parber on October 16, 1947, in San Francisco, California, and grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area, spending some time going to school in Colorado, where he met future Grateful Dead member John Perry Barlow.
Weir started playing guitar at age 13 and gravitated to a local bluegrass scene, where he first encountered Jerry Garcia playing banjo.
On December 31, 1965, Garcia and Weir agreed to form their own group called Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions, which evolved into the Grateful Dead.
Weir played rhythm guitar, and sang for the group, for decades.

He also explored a solo career and variety of other groups outside of the Grateful Dead starting in the 1970s, including Kingfish, Bobby and the Midnites, RatDog, Furthur, The Other Ones, The Dead, Wolf Bros, and Dead & Company.
All groups featured fellow Grateful Dead collaborators and explored genres from country rock to jam band to jazz-influenced roots rock with a basis in blues and country.

His vocal contributions were mostly only harmonies and as a backup singer, but he took lead on several tracks, including Grateful Dead anthem "Truckin'", a song noted by the Library of Congress as a national treasure in 1997.

Outside of musical performance, Weir has also established Tamalpais Research Institute, a virtual performance platform, and was active in politics, advocating for several causes, including environmentalism, poverty relief, and issues related to the arts.
He had stayed active in the Bay Area music scene, performing live with local musicians and co-owning the venue Sweetwater Music Hall in Mill Valley, California.
He is survived by wife Natascha and daughters Chloe and Monet, as well as other family.

items.title: Boy retrieves Nintendo Switch locked away in gun safe, and shoots his father

s: On January 13, the night of his 11th birthday, a boy allegedly shot his father with a gun retrieved from a gun safe in the family's home in Duncannon Borough, Pennsylvania.
According to court documents, the boy told investigators he became mad after his father told him to go to bed.
Police charged the boy with criminal homicide.
The court has refused bail.
The boy was placed in Perry County Prison, and an initial court hearing was scheduled for January 22, according to a criminal docket.
According to court documents, the mother was asleep until the gunshot woke her.
When state police arrived at the home, the boy was heard shouting "Daddy's dead" and was overheard telling his mother, "I killed Daddy."
Police arrived on scene around 3:20 a.m.
Eastern Standard Time (08:20 UTC).
According to the affidavit, the boy told the police that he did not think about what would happen after the shot, saying he was "mad and did not think about that."

According to court documents, the boy told investigators he found a key to the gun safe in a drawer and unlocked the safe in an attempt to get back his Nintendo Switch, then loaded the gun and shot his father.
The Nintendo Switch had been placed in a gun safe located in the parents' bedroom.
The parents adopted the boy in 2018, according to a report by the New York Post.

items.title: Bruce Gallanter interviews Elliott Sharp, Joe Fonda at Downtown Music Gallery event

s: On January 12, Downtown Music Gallery in New York City hosted a public reading and discussion featuring Elliott Sharp and Joe Fonda, followed by their first-ever live performance together as a duo.
The event also included extended, in-person interviews conducted by Bruce Gallanter focused on the artists’ recently published books.
Sharp read first from his new book, Feedback: Translations from the IrRational, and was then interviewed by Gallanter.
Fonda then discussed passages from his new book, My Life in the World of Music.
After these talks, Sharp and Fonda, who have known each other since 1978, performed together using a variety of extended techniques.
Sharp played his electroacoustic guitar through an amplifier, while Fonda played acoustic contrabass with no amplification.
Note: This interview has been edited for clarity.
((Bruce Gallanter)) : Elliott, I have a few questions for you.
((Elliott Sharp)) : Okay, if we have time.
((Gallanter)) Yeah.
When did you pick up the guitar?
((Gallanter)) And you would listen to mostly rock music at that point?
((Sharp)) Yeah, and classical music.
I played classical piano as a kid and classical clarinet after that when I was eight, when the piano gave me asthma (in my interpretation) that nearly killed me.
So I played clarinet, then I got an electric guitar, and that was it.
The clarinet went by the wayside.

Also, I got kicked out of wind ensemble and marching band because I came back from a summer residency after my junior year with long hair and a beard, and Al Renino, the band director, would have none of that.
((Gallanter)) When you first started playing, were you playing kind of blues rock stuff at the beginning?

((Sharp)) Well, making psychedelic noise, I was very inspired by readings I was doing in Cage, I was an electronics geek, so I was building my own circuits and experimenting with tape delays and building ring modulators and fuzz, so I was making a lot of noise... and trying to learn Jeff Beck's guitar playing from the Yardbirds records and then Jimi Hendrix.
I mean, Jeff Beck's playing, at least I could find the notes.
With Hendrix, it was beyond me at first, it was just so sonic, you know, but yeah, and a lot of blues, country blues, playing a lot of slide.
((Gallanter)) So you played in blues rock bands?
((Sharp)) Yeah.
I was playing, the first blues band I was in was called the MFBB, the MotherFucking Blues Band, and I was playing bass in that.
((Sharp)) That was '68, '69 when I was still in high school.
I started playing guitar and pedal steel in bands in Ithaca in 1970 when I was at Cornell.
((Gallanter)) OK.
That's where you went to school first?

((Gallanter)) So you've had I mean, I know that most people think of you more as avant-garde kind of noisemaker, even with the guitar and the other instruments that you play, but it seems that you've always had that blues thing.
((Sharp)) Yeah, blues.
And I went for a long period of playing bebop and studying with Roswell Rudd.
But I'll still do gigs occasionally, playing like for a party, playing some blues or jazz or funk tunes, and people come and say, well, I didn't know you actually knew how to play guitar.
((Gallanter)) Somebody said the same thing today when we had on that Terraplane CD.
They said, this is Elliott Sharp?
He plays the blues?
I said, he plays the blues really well, and he's obviously studied it, because you've been doing records of that, starting with that Hoosegow record.

items.title: White House deletes Truth Social post portraying Obamas as apes

s: The White House has deleted a post on Donald Trump's social media account containing a video portraying former United States President Barack Obama and his wife Michelle Obama as apes.
The video triggered a backlash from American politicians, including from Trump's own Republican Party.
After initially defending the post, the White House removed the post from Trump's account in response to backlash, according to the BBC.
A White House official stated that a staff member had mistakenly posted the video.
Trump himself has stated that he did not see the full video prior to it being posted and according to ABC News Australia, he refused to apologize, stating "I didn't make a mistake.
I mean, I give - I look at a lot - thousands of things."
Senator Tim Scott, who is both African American and a Republican, referred to the video as "the most racist thing I've ever seen out of this White House."
The video, which lasts 62 seconds, used the song The Lion Sleeps Tonight as background music and references allegations of electoral fraud in the 2020 United States presidential election.

In addition to the Obamas, it portrays various other Democratic Party politicians as animals, such as United States Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of New York City, and former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton.
Former United States President Joe Biden, like the Obamas, is portrayed as an ape eating a banana.
According to the BBC, the video is believed to have originated from conservative meme creator Xerias, who shared the post on X in October 2025.

items.title: Göbeklitepe, Taş Tepeler and life 12,000 years ago exhibition opens in Berlin, Germany

s: On February 6, 2026, the "Gebaute Gemeinschaft - Göbeklitepe, Taş Tepeler and Life 12,000 Years Ago" exhibition opened at Berlin's James-Simon-Galerie.
Scheduled to be running until July 19, 2026, the show featured 93 archaeological artifacts brought from Turkey from Göbeklitepe and the Taş Tepeler region.
Stone sculptures from the UNESCO World Heritage site Göbeklitepe were exhibited alongside finds from Karahantepe, Sayburç, and Çakmaktepe.
Everyday objects and jewelry were on display.

Spanish photographer Isabel Muñoz's contemporary interpretations framing the hunter-gatherers' transition to settled life across eight thematic sections, which were exhibited in Spain earlier in 2024, were also included in the exhibition.
The exhibition was curated by Barbara Helwing (Vorderasiatisches Museum) and Necmi Karul (Istanbul University) in collaboration with Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum and the Taş Tepeler research project.
It was the first time some exhibits were brought abroad, after having been exhibited in several locations in Turkey.

items.title: Caloundra through to next round of 2026 Australia Cup preliminaries

s: Caloundra have qualified for the next round of soccer's Australia Cup qualifiers with a 4-1 win over Pacific Pines on Saturday night in Meridan Plains, Queensland.
"[We had a] good second half," said Caloundra captain Kaine Frew.
"Obviously first competitive match [of the year] tonight.
It was good for the boys to get the cobwebs out.
We've played a few easier sort of preseason games and obviously they've come up from the Gold Coast."
Three goals in the space of ten minutes secured Caloundra's advancement after the scores were tied at 1 all at half time.
"We started a bit slow and obviously we got a few new players," Frew said.
"So we're all just still gelling.
But yeah, no, it was a really good second half.
We're happy with that.
And we'll take that into training next week and be ready for round one."
Caloundra's next game is scheduled to be against Brisbane Knights as part of the Football Queensland Premier League 2 opening round on February 28.
"[Brisbane Kights are] a big club, but we really don't know [what to expect], to be honest," said Frew.
"We're just going to worry about ourselves.
Obviously, we think we can be competitive this year there's no doubt about that.
As long as we can play 90 minutes.
Not like tonight where, you know, first half an hour wasn't great.
We need to play like we did in the second half for the whole game."

items.title: Musical performance presented by Striped Light in Long Island City, New York showcases four performers

s: On the evening of February 16, 2026, an audience gathered at an undisclosed location to see a performance by three experimental musical acts in Long Island City, Queens, New York, as part of the ongoing Striped Light series of events.
A volunteer contributor to Wikinews attended the event as a reporter.
There were somewhere between forty and a hundred people in attendance.
The doors opened for the event at 7:30 p.m.
New York time (0030 UTC).
Jennifer Gersten played the first set, as a soloist.
She played the violin using a variety of techniques, holding it in a traditional manner as well as on her lap at times.
Jack Langdon played the second set, also as a soloist.
He played a Native American flute through amplification, taking advantage of the opportunity to explore extended techniques and unusual sounds with the flute.
John King and Leyya Mona Tawil performed the third set as a duo.

King played guitar while using electronics and a laptop positioned on a table in front of him, while Tawil worked with electronics, multiple microphones, and unconventional objects; at one point, she danced on the amplified stage.
In contrast to the earlier sets, this was a high-volume set.
Striped Light is an ongoing series curated by David Watson and Ian Douglas-Moore.
The location of the performances is only revealed to performers and people who purchase tickets.

items.title: Green Party wins major by-election in northern England city of Manchester

s: The Green Party of England and Wales candidate Hannah Spencer has been declared the winner of Thursday's by-election in Gorton and Denton, a parliamentary constituency in Manchester, which was triggered following the resignation of the previous Labour MP Andrew Gwynne.
The election marks the first parliamentary by-election won by a Green Party candidate, and the first Green Party election win in the North of England.
Spencer will become the fifth current Green Party MP, with just under 41% of the vote, a lead of 12% on the second-place candidate, Matt Goodwin of Reform UK, who received just under 29% of the vote.
The election was highly anticipated as a test of confidence for the current Labour government, which has seen numerous high-profile scandals over past months.
The Labour candidate received 25% of the vote, dropping 25% from the 50% won at the 2024 general election.
The seat was previously regarded as the sixth safest seat for the party in Britain, and had not been lost by a Labour Party candidate since 1931.

Mayor of Greater Manchester Andy Burnham had applied to stand as the party's candidate, but was blocked by its National Executive Committee over a worry that Labour would lose the resulting by-election for Mayor, and amid fears he would mount a leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

Former Deputy Leader of the Labour Party and former Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner said that "This result must be a wake up call" amid the election adding to mounting internal party pressure on Keir Starmer to resign following the election, which would trigger a leadership election within his party.
